required_fixes: The frozen target list in spec.json identity_resolution.frozen_target_list freezes expected_authors=['TBD'] for ActivityFrames (the PC-COST-ACCOUNTING target), making prereg 4.1 condition 3 (author substring match) unsatisfiable. This is a frozen corpus defect, not a resolver failure. A director mandate must either: (a) replace ['TBD'] with the actual author list ['Iyamu', 'Nossa'] for that entry, or (b) add an 'author list unavailable' branch to the identity rule that permits pass when expected_authors is ['TBD'], before any field extraction occurs.

The frozen target list contains 3 undeclared identifier defects (BrowserGym 2401.15378v2, MiniWoB++ 1802.08827v3, SeeAct 2402.04566v2) that resolve to unrelated real papers. A director mandate must authorize an identifier repair pass whose only permitted mutation is replacing a frozen arXiv ID that provably resolves to an unrelated artifact, with every repair logged and the identity rule unchanged.

The frozen target list of 14 entries is a list of benchmarks and environments, not persistent-state web agents. None of the 5 correctly resolved targets reports persistent state across sessions or episodes. The Part 1 construct population within the corpus is 0. A director mandate must restate the Part 1 target population as systems that actually persist state across sessions or episodes and authorize a corpus search for that population.

The bounded snowball (prereg 4.4) yielded 0 usable candidates because the frozen inclusion rule requires arXiv identifiers inside reference strings and the PC artifact prints none. A director mandate must permit the snowball to resolve reference entries by author-title-year against the Semantic Scholar graph API (which returned HTTP 200 on the substrate probe), with the identity rule unchanged.

The title condition reading (DEV-3) must be ruled on by a director. The primary test uses case-insensitive substring plus expected-token coverage >= 0.85; the alternative strict full-token-set Jaccard >= 0.85 reading would make identity_resolution_recall = 0.0. Both readings are logged per target; the director must designate which is binding for future packets.
validity_findings: VF1: The frozen design (spec.json, prereg.md, freeze.json) is integrity-verified. All three frozen input hashes match their recomputed values (provenance.json frozen_inputs_verified_unmodified).

VF2: The experiment correctly executes the frozen protocol: transport probes logged, identity resolution applied deterministically, four controls run, field determinations quote-backed, frozen gates evaluated in precedence order. No outcome-bearing measurement was inspected before the frozen rule was applied.

VF3: Gate 1 (PC-COST-ACCOUNTING fails) fires and is the binding MEASUREMENT_INVALID trigger for the entire experiment. The failure is in the frozen target list: expected_authors=['TBD'] for ActivityFrames makes prereg 4.1 condition 3 unsatisfiable. The resolver correctly records pass=null (unevaluable), not pass=false. The artifact itself is real and correct (C1, C2, C4 pass).

VF4: Gate 2 (NC-REAL-BUT-WRONG fails to flag) does NOT fire. The null control retrieves a REAL artifact (1802.05012v2, a 2018 paper on literary-fiction authorship), the resolver flags C2_title_mismatch and C3_author_mismatch, emits AMBIGUOUS -> UNMEASURED, and does NOT score NOT_FOUND. The domain-keyword condition C4 passes (abstract contains 'agent'), demonstrating the conjunction has power.

VF5: Gate 3 (any target scored NOT_FOUND) does NOT fire. Zero rows in the artifact table carry resolution_status=NOT_FOUND or scored_as=NOT_FOUND. All 11 unresolved targets are scored UNMEASURED with explicit absence evidence. This corrects the parent packet's failure mode.

VF6: Gate 4 (PC-PERFORMANCE-ENVELOPE fails) does NOT fire. WebVoyager (2401.13919v4) resolves CORRECTLY_RESOLVED and all 4 required fields (success_rate, denominator, evaluation_convention, benchmark_split) are extracted with evidence quotes.

VF7: Gate 5 (identity_resolution_recall < 0.6) fires. Recall = 5/14 = 0.357143. The metric is not denominator-invariant: excluding the 5 prereg-declared placeholders gives 5/9 = 0.555556; over the 8 entries with real author lists gives 5/8 = 0.625. The frozen gate uses the 14-entry denominator for all three parts, though no per-part partition of the frozen list exists.

VF8: The coverage metric (identity_resolution_recall) conflates corpus design errors (placeholder author lists, wrong identifiers) with resolver failure. It measures name-to-artifact identity, not Part 1 construct coverage (persistent-state web agents). The derived count p1_n_correctly_resolved_targets_persisting_state_across_sessions = 0 (VN-5).

VF9: Deviations from frozen design are documented in provenance.json (DEV-1 through DEV-6). DEV-1 (arXiv abs/PDF transport vs blocked Atom API) and DEV-2 (base-ID re-probe for 404s) are transport-only, do not weaken identity conditions. DEV-3 (title condition reading) is an interpretation of an ambiguous frozen sentence; both Jaccard and coverage values are logged per target so the decision is auditable and reversible. DEV-4 (snowball attempted, 0 candidates) does not substitute retrieval. DEV-5 (pypdf install) is environment. DEV-6 (artifacts at repo paths with sha256, not pinned to commit) is a branch-discipline constraint. No deviation weakens a preregistered condition.

VF10: PDF text-layer representation loss (VN-8) is acknowledged: ligatures dropped, de-hyphenation, tables not linearised. AgentBench-web headline rate reported as NOT_REPORTED rather than a number because numeric table cells may not be linearised. Every absence determination records retrieval scope and character count searched.

VF11: All recorded quantities carry modeled_vs_measured labels, denominators, accounting conventions, and stated uncertainties per the output contract. Modeled quantities are explicitly labeled 'modeled' with modeling assumptions stated in accounting_convention (e.g., 'NUMERATOR MODELED... upper bound'). No modeled quantity is reported as a bound on SPIDER's economics.

VF12: Part 2 reveals 4 distinct evaluation conventions across 4 benchmarks (WebArena/WebVoyager shared Task Success Rate; Mind2Web with ground-truth action history; WebShop Task Score = 100×avg reward; AgentBench per-environment SR). No common denominator enabling direct comparison exists. WebVoyager explicitly states it follows WebArena convention, so those two are comparable to each other.

VF13: Part 3 evidence comes only from ActivityFrames §6.2, which varies WRITE representation (raw JSON, compiled schema, compact block, LLM summary) while holding RETRIEVED CONTEXT CONSTANT. It reports no retrieval quality metric (recall, precision, nDCG, hit rate, MRR). The ablation result 'write_pipeline_only_retrieval_held_constant' cannot support a retrieval-vs-write variance decomposition.

VF14: The experiment status=MEASUREMENT_INVALID, outcome=NOT_APPLICABLE correctly encodes that no scientific verdict is licensed. The frozen gates fire before any SUPPORTS/FALSIFIES/MIXED/INCONCLUSIVE assignment. This is a measurement-validity failure, NOT a scientific falsification and NOT an infrastructure failure.
baseline_findings: BF1: B-COLD-BROWSING and B-DETERMINISTIC-EXECUTOR baselines are not tested in this intel experiment (prereg section 10 excludes reproduction and SPIDER's own measurements). The baselines remain as conceptual anchors in the spec but are not operationalized here.
BF2: B-RAG-INSTRUCTIONS and B-PUBLISHED-NUMBERS-ONLY are similarly conceptual. The experiment reads published numbers only; it does not reproduce or compare against a RAG baseline.

BF3: The positive control PC-COST-ACCOUNTING was intended as the primary instrument calibration for Part 1. Its failure means the instrument is not calibrated against a known source that reports the target construct. No alternative calibration was performed.

BF4: The null control NC-REAL-BUT-WRONG passes and demonstrates the identity gate has specificity against real-but-wrong artifacts. This is the key improvement over the parent packet where 5 wrong artifacts were scored NOT_FOUND.

claim_ceiling: This packet establishes that the frozen instrument fails its own positive control due to a frozen corpus defect (expected_authors=['TBD'] for the PC target). Within the corpus actually reached (5 correctly resolved benchmarks + 1 memory paper), no published artifact reports a measured break-even reuse count f* with denominator, accounting convention, and uncertainty, and no published artifact shows persistent cross-episode state beating re-derivation on a real, billed cost basis. The one artifact reporting the cost-accounting construct (ActivityFrames) explicitly reserves live billing, states its modeled numerator is an upper bound, and reports its single live in-loop saving as ~14% against a modeled 83.3%. The Part 2 envelope shows 4 incompatible evaluation conventions across 4 benchmarks, with only WebArena↔WebVoyager sharing a convention. Part 3 yields no retrieval-vs-write variance decomposition; the single ablation varies write pipeline at fixed retrieval. All recorded quantities are at claim ceiling: 'verbatim from a named artifact, denominators exposed, modeled quantities labelled'. No literature-level prevalence estimate is offered. C-PRODUCT-ECON remains without external justification from this packet, and this packet does not establish that such justification is absent in the broader literature.

unresolved: U-1: Whether any published web-agent system anywhere reports a MEASURED break-even reuse count f* with denominator, accounting convention, and uncertainty remains genuinely unknown. The searched corpus was 5 benchmarks + 1 memory paper; no prevalence estimate is offered.

U-2: The correct arXiv identifiers for BrowserGym, MiniWoB++, and SeeAct are unknown to this run. The smallest unblocking action is a director mandate permitting an identifier repair pass (only mutation: replace frozen arXiv ID that provably resolves to unrelated artifact; identity rule unchanged; every repair logged).

U-3: The Part 1 construct population inside the frozen list is 0. The smallest unblocking action is a director mandate restating the Part 1 target population as systems that actually persist state across sessions/episodes and authorizing a corpus search for that population.

U-4: The bounded snowball could not execute under its frozen inclusion rule (no arXiv IDs in PC artifact's reference list). The smallest unblocking action is a director mandate permitting resolution of reference entries by author-title-year against Semantic Scholar graph API (HTTP 200 on substrate probe), identity rule unchanged.

U-5: The director must rule on the title-condition reading (DEV-3). The primary test (substring + token coverage >= 0.85) gives recall 0.357; the strict full-token-set Jaccard >= 0.85 gives recall 0.0. Both are logged per target; this decision does not change the overall MEASUREMENT_INVALID (gate 1 is independent) but affects Parts 2/3 INCONCLUSIVE basis.

U-6: Whether the Part 2 spread (1.1% to 59.1%) is a real capability spread or an artifact of the frozen list's benchmark-era composition and heterogeneous model tiers/date ranges is unknown. None of the 5 correctly resolved artifacts is a memory-augmented or workflow-inducing agent, so the mandate's actual comparison target was not reached.

U-7: Whether the arXiv Atom API 406 (OBS-1) is persistent or runner-specific is unknown. It does not affect this packet's validity (abs/PDF transport succeeded) but affects any future design freezing the Atom endpoint as its retrieval channel.

U-8: The reusable identity-resolution instrument, frozen matching rule, and four controls are published as code plus raw evidence at exact repository-relative paths with sha256 hashes (provenance.json artifact_index, result.json artifacts). They are NOT published at an exact commit because branch discipline forbids git commit in this session.
